title: Local parameter criterion for a strict normal crossings boundary
statement: Let $X$ be a regular Noetherian scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and let $H\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $H$ is a strict normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] if and only if for every $x\in X$ there are a regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters] and $0\le r\le d$ such that the stalk of the ideal of $H$ is $(t_1\cdots t_r)$. The empty product is $1$, so the case $r=0$ describes a point off $H$ and includes the empty boundary. In particular this local equation condition implies that $H$ is reduced and effective Cartier and that its finitely many reduced irreducible components have regular scheme-theoretic intersections of the expected codimensions, as required by the boundary definition.

source.place: Tags 0BI9 (definition-strict-normal-crossings) and 0BIA (lemma-strict-normal-crossings), including the proof from regular intersections to local parameter equations; compare ILO VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), printed pp.118--119. Since X itself is regular, the off-divisor condition is automatic.

proof.text: Assume first that H is a strict normal crossings boundary. Fix x in X and put A = O_{X,x}, d = dim A. List the boundary components through x as C_1,...,C_r. The boundary definition says that A/I_i is regular local of dimension d-1 for the ideal I_i of C_i, because each C_i is regular and has codimension one. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters] to I_i: it is generated by an initial sublist of a regular system of parameters. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], the quotient by a sublist of length c_i has dimension d-c_i. Hence c_i=1, so I_i=(t_i) for a parameter t_i in A.

source.place: Tags 0BI9 and 0BIA; the component-to-local-parameter argument, together with Algebra Tags 00NR and 00NQ.

proof.text: For any subset J of the components through x, let I_J=(t_i : i in J). Its quotient is the local ring of the corresponding scheme-theoretic intersection, hence is regular of dimension d-|J| by the boundary hypothesis. The kernel of the cotangent map m_A/m_A^2 -> (m_A/I_J)/(m_A/I_J)^2 is (I_J+m_A^2)/m_A^2, and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] gives this kernel dimension |J|. The classes of the t_i span it, so they are independent; extend them to a basis and lift the remaining vectors. [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] then gives a generating set of m_A, i.e. a regular system of parameters containing all the t_i. Since A is regular local, [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization] applies to this system. If h generates the effective Cartier ideal of H at x, reducedness makes its prime factorization square-free, and the minimal primes are exactly the (t_i) for components through x. Thus h is a unit times t_1...t_r. Away from H the empty product is 1. This proves the local product condition.

source.place: Tags 00KU, 00NQ and 00NR; Tag 0AG0 for the regular-local UFD factorization; the intersection criterion is Tag 0BIA.

proof.text: Conversely assume the stated product equation at every x. In A=O_{X,x}, a regular system of parameters is a regular sequence by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], and A is a domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. Therefore the product t_1...t_r is a nonzerodivisor, so the local ideal of H is effective Cartier. By [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization], each t_i is prime and the principal ideal of the product is radical; its local minimal primes are exactly (t_i). For every subset J of these factors, the quotient A/(t_i:i in J) is regular local of dimension d-|J| by the same regular-sequence statement. Thus the local irreducible components are regular and every scheme-theoretic intersection is regular of the required codimension. These local assertions glue, while Noetherianity gives finitely many global irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components]. Hence H satisfies the strict normal crossings boundary definition.

source.place: Tags 0BI9 and 0BIA; the converse from local parameter equations to regular intersections.

proof.text: The empty-product case r=0 gives the unit ideal at points outside H and the empty boundary when it occurs everywhere. The preceding arguments also show that the local equation is reduced and Cartier and that all component intersections have the dimensions required in the statement, so the final ‘in particular’ clauses follow directly.

split_report.summary: Audited the imported criterion against Stacks Tags 0BI9 and 0BIA. Step 1: regular C_i of codimension 1, then 00NR quotient-kernel, then 00NQ dimension d-c, which forces I_i=(t_i). Step 2: the cotangent kernel of A to A/I_J has dimension |J|, and Nakayama extends the t_i to one parameter system. With the UFD node and the radical ideal, the minimal primes of h are the (t_i), using the definition's statement that the C_i are the reduced irreducible components. So h = unit*t_1...t_r. Step 3: the product of parameters is a nonzerodivisor (domain and regular sequence) and radical (pairwise non-associate primes). The components' stalk ideals are (t_j), and quotients by any subset are regular of dimension d-|J| (00NQ permutation clause). Finitely many components because H is Noetherian; all conditions are stalkwise and Cartier spreads out. Step 4 is genuinely elementary. lean.statement: theorem isStrictNormalCrossingsBoundary_iff_parameters (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (_hX : IsRegularScheme X) (H : X.IdealSheafData) : IsStrictNormalCrossingsBoundary H ↔ ∀ x : X, ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (hx : x ∈ U.1) (t : List (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (r : ℕ), IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters t ∧ r ≤ t.length ∧ (H.ideal U).map (X.presheaf.germ U.1 x hx).hom = Ideal.span {(t.take r).prod}
